facts.text: District Collector, Municipal Commissioner, Finance Secretary and Divisional Commissioner are civil servants in the government's administrative system.
facts.quote: a few posts like District Collector, Municipal Commissioner, Finance Secretary, and Divisional Commissioner are mentioned. These are civil servants in the government's administrative system.

facts.text: The Prime Minister and his Council of Ministers make proposals for new laws and decide upon policies.
facts.quote: the Prime Minister and his Council of Ministers make proposals for new laws and also decide upon policies.

facts.text: Bureaucracy is the administrative system which works under the Union Executive and has the responsibility of actual implementation of government's policies.
facts.quote: 'Bureaucracy' is the administrative system which works under the Union Executive and has the responsibility of actual implementation of government's policies.

facts.text: The government carries out two fundamental functions: defending the country and ensuring safety of citizens, and providing services to citizens to ease their daily lives.
facts.quote: (1) To defend the country from external aggression and internal threats and to ensure safety of citizen. (2) To provide various services to citizens and ease their daily lives

facts.text: The first function, security of the country, is carried out by the defence forces; their role in internal security is as aid to civil services.
facts.quote: The first function is to ensure security of the country. This is carried out by the service called the defence forces. The role of internal security is carried out as aid to civil services.

facts.text: For the second function an administrative system called the 'civil services' is developed; the system of civil servants is also known as bureaucracy.
facts.quote: For the second function, an administrative system is developed. We call it the 'civil services'. The system of civil servants is also known as bureaucracy.

facts.text: In the Parliamentary democracy, representatives elected by the people and the ministers have the responsibility of administration; government functions are discharged by departments.
facts.quote: In the Parliamentary democracy, representatives elected by the people and the ministers have the responsibility of administration. The functions of government are discharged by various departments.

facts.text: Every department has a minister who is its political head; the minister gives priority to public welfare and, though maybe not an expert, is conscious of broad public interest.
facts.quote: Every department has a minister who is the political head of that department. ... The minister may not be expert in a particular subject but he/she is conscious of broad public interest.

facts.text: The Secretary of the department gives expert advice to the ministers; secretaries are appointed from the civil service.
facts.quote: The Secretary of the department gives expert advice to the ministers. The secretaries are appointed from the civil service.

facts.text: The aspirations of the people and administrative expertise are put in harmony in the parliamentary system.
facts.quote: The aspirations of the people and administrative expertise are thus put in harmony in the parliamentary system.

facts.text: Bureaucracy is a permanent mechanism: tax collection, environment protection, law and order and social security are done consistently; ministers change after every election but the bureaucracy remains constant.
facts.quote: Tax collection, environment protection, maintenance of law and order, provisions regarding social security are certain important tasks that have to be consistently undertaken by the bureaucracy. This is possible because bureaucracy is a permanent mechanism. The Prime Minister and their Council of Ministers change after every election but the bureaucracy under their control remains constant.

facts.text: Political neutrality: whatever party is in power, the bureaucracy implements its policy decisions with the same efficiency and commitment, and civil servants should not take a political stand.
facts.quote: The bureaucracy is politically neutral. This means that regardless of the political party in power, the bureaucracy is supposed to carry out the implementation of their policy decisions with the same efficiency and commitment. In this regard, the civil servants should abstain from taking a political stand

facts.text: If a party loses elections, another party comes to power and may change some policies; even then the bureaucracy must remain neutral.
facts.quote: If a political party fails to win elections, it has to leave government and another party that wins elections comes to power. The new government may change some policies of the earlier government. Even in such case, the bureaucracy is expected to remain neutral while discharging its duties.

facts.text: Anonymity: a civil service is not held directly responsible for any success or failure of policy; the Minister, as head of the department, is accountable, and civil servants are never publicly criticised.
facts.quote: Anonymity means that a civil service should not be held directly responsible for any success or failure of policy. It is the Minister who is responsible ... Civil servants are never publicly criticised.

facts.text: The Parliament holds the Minister responsible for malpractices; the Minister bears the responsibility and protects the bureaucracy.
facts.quote: The Parliament holds the Minister responsible for malpractices. In such case the Minister bears the responsibility and protects the bureaucracy.

facts.text: The structure of the Indian bureaucracy is extensive and complex; post-independence reforms were implemented by the bureaucratic structure.
facts.quote: The structure of the Indian bureaucracy is extensive and complex. Several important reforms that were introduced during the post-independence period have been effectively implemented by the bureaucratic structure.

facts.text: Bureaucracy gives stability to the political system by consistently providing everyday services like water supply, transport, electricity and public cleanliness.
facts.quote: Bureaucracy gives stability to the political system. Water supply, transport, electricity, public cleanliness, health, agricultural reforms, prevention of pollution and such other services are every day needs of the people and need to be consistently provided to them.

facts.text: Bureaucracy is an important instrument of social transformation: laws for empowerment of women, child security and plans for the marginalised are implemented by it.
facts.quote: bureaucracy is an important instrument of social transformation. The laws enacted by the government for empowerment of women, child security, plans for the marginalised sections are implemented by the bureaucracy.

facts.text: In the democratisation of society, marginalised sections were brought into the mainstream by implementing the reservation policy, increasing their participation in decision making. Democratisation needs progressive laws and policies and also the effective participation of bureaucracy.
facts.quote: Marginalised sections of society have been brought into mainstream by implementing the reservation policy. Their participation has been increased in the process of decision making. ... Democratisation of society not only requires progressive laws and policies it also needs the effective participation of bureaucracy.

facts.text: In India there are three main types of civil services.
facts.quote: In India, there are three main types of civil services

facts.text: All-India Services include the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS) and Indian Forest Service.
facts.quote: They include the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS) and Indian Forest Service (IFS).

facts.text: Union or Central Services come under the Union Government and include Indian Foreign Service and Indian Revenue Service (IRS).
facts.quote: They come under the Union Government. They include Indian Foreign Service (IFS), Indian Revenue Service (IRS) etc.

facts.text: State Civil Services come under the State Government and include Deputy District Collector, Block Development Officer and Tehsildar (Executive Magistrate); they are recruited through State-level competitive examinations.
facts.quote: They come under the State Government. They include Deputy District Collector, Block Development Officer, Tehsildar (Executive Magistrate) etc. They are recruited through competitive examinations held at the State-level.

facts.text: The Constitution established autonomous institutions like the Public Service Commissions so that civil servants are selected on merit and efficiency.
facts.quote: Indian constitution has established autonomous institutions like the Public Service Commissions to ensure that the civil servants are selected on the basis of criteria of merit and efficiency.

facts.text: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) conducts examinations for recruitment and appointment for All-India Services and Central Services.
facts.quote: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) conducts examinations for recruitment and appointment of candidates for All-India Services and Central Services.

facts.text: The Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) selects candidates through competitive examinations and recommends them for recruitment in the state administration.
facts.quote: The Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) selects candidates through competitive examinations and recommends them to the government to be recruited in the state administration.

facts.text: There are reservations in civil services for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Women, Other Backward Castes and specially-abled, so weaker sections are not left out due to social inequality.
facts.quote: there is a provision for reservations for the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Women, Other Backward Castes and specially-abled. This provision ensures that weaker sections of the society are not left out of civil services due to social inequality.

facts.text: The efficiency of a department depends on the inter-relationship between the Minister and the Department Secretaries and Deputy Secretaries.
facts.quote: The efficiency of a particular government department depends upon the inter-relationship between the Minister and Department Secretaries and Deputy Secretaries.

facts.text: Decisions are made by the minister, but civil servants give the information, control it, know the financial provisions and the history of policies; so ministers depend on civil servants.
facts.quote: The decisions relating to the department are made by concerned minister but necessary information to make such decisions is given by the civil servants. ... Hence, ministers are dependent upon the civil servants.

facts.text: If ministers keep a dialogue with civil servants and build mutual trust and transparency, it helps the departments.
facts.quote: If ministers maintain a dialogue with civil servants and develop mutual trust and transparency, it will help the departments.
